helper.content:
export function appendCppMapEntries(lines: string[]): void {
  lines.push(
    `// Each invocation owns its captured map values until canonical encoding finishes.`,
    `// Small maps avoid a vector allocation; larger maps retain bounded reservation.`,
    `class RustraMapEntries {`,
    `public:`,
    `  using Entry = std::pair<std::string, jsi::Value>;`,
    `  RustraMapEntries(jsi::Runtime& rt, size_t count) : use_inline_(count <= inline_entries_.size()) {`,
    `    if (count > heap_entries_.max_size()) throw jsi::JSError(rt, "rustra: map size exceeds native capacity");`,
    `    if (!use_inline_) heap_entries_.reserve(std::min<size_t>(count, 64));`,
    `  }`,
    `  void emplace_back(std::string&& key, jsi::Value&& value) {`,
    `    if (use_inline_) inline_entries_[size_] = Entry(std::move(key), std::move(value));`,
    `    else heap_entries_.emplace_back(std::move(key), std::move(value));`,
    `    ++size_;`,
    `  }`,
    `  Entry* begin() { return use_inline_ ? inline_entries_.data() : heap_entries_.data(); }`,
    `  Entry* end() { return begin() + size_; }`,
    `  size_t size() const { return size_; }`,
    `private:`,
    `  std::array<Entry, 4> inline_entries_;`,
    `  std::vector<Entry> heap_entries_;`,
    `  size_t size_ = 0;`,
    `  bool use_inline_;`,
    `};`,
    ``,
  );
}

# Task 3 small-map candidate review

Decision: **accepted for parent-owned A/B and full native/public verification; no actionable correctness or specification blocker found.** This is source-review acceptance, not performance adoption or Nitro parity acceptance.

Reviewed against `docs/plans/2026-09-16-nitro-parity-followup.md` Task 3 and global constraints, the candidate report, and the frozen before/candidate artifacts. Worktree HEAD is `ae30d7640fcb6a9954940ec5a0875028bf70d31e`. The scoped working diff and new helper were reviewed directly. The parent explicitly admits the separate bare RN generated drift refresh. No code changes, builds, test execution, benchmarks, or delegation were performed by this reviewer; only this report was written.

## Standards and correctness

**0 actionable findings.**

- `generate-cpp-map-entries.ts` uses ordinary `std::array`, `std::vector`, `std::string`, and owning `jsi::Value` lifetimes. The installed JSI header gives `Value` an undefined default constructor and noexcept move operations. No borrowed key/value pointer, manual lifetime management, or cross-invocation cache was introduced. Throwing getters unwind both containers normally; already captured JSI roots survive reentry and collection.
- The single production insertion site captures `_count` once, constructs storage from that same count, and appends exactly once for each `_j < _count`. Thus inline indices are 0–3, sorting/iteration cover only initialized entries, and the empty range uses the non-null array storage. Above four entries, sorting is reached only after successful insertion, so the heap range is nonempty. Exceptions exit before sorting. The existing vector `max_size()` guard and error text remain; initial heap reservation is still `min(count, 64)`.
- Enumeration, normalized UTF-8 lookup, value capture, canonical `std::string` byte comparison, and each value writer remain textually equivalent. Sorting moves owned entries after all getters have run. The helper introduces no JS invocation during sorting. Invalid primitive values still fail at the original conversion point.
- The seven existing primitive map kinds use the same branch and value pushers. `PostcardFieldKind`, command support analysis, unknown-kind default, complex-map generation, and decoding are unchanged. This does not silently promote unknown maps or change supported types.
- Direct includes make the helper self-contained with the existing JSI/header context. The shared helper centralizes storage policy without changing public interfaces. No documented compatibility invariant violation or actionable smell was identified.

## Specification and provenance

**0 actionable findings.**

- The production RN C++ diff contains the helper/includes and five entry-container substitutions only, including ordinary `resourceOpen` and `scoreTotal` commands. It has no benchmark field-name condition. The contract hash and RN header are unchanged. The general optimization preserves the fixture, algorithms, bridge guards, ownership, payload admission, Promise behavior, and existing dispatch paths.
- All eight archived baseline hashes and all 17 archived candidate hashes match their recorded values. All 17 candidate files also match the live worktree. Both RN manifests' 24 listed artifacts match their recorded hashes. The bare RN C++/header now match the current RN equivalents; its refreshed adapter paths resolve to this worktree's installed native package. The larger bare RN regeneration remains separate maintenance, and its stale before-codec must not be used as an equivalent performance baseline.
- Existing supplied evidence is sufficient for this review stage: CLI test compile succeeded, 17 targeted generator tests passed, both RN `codegen --check` runs passed, and the parent-owned actual-Hermes result log reports **1,129 assertions, 0 failures**. The final native source identities include the reviewed candidate C++ and test include. These checks were not rerun.
- The initial four identical baseline/candidate failures were attributed to the harness's disabled block scoping. The new getter factories capture distinct function parameters while retaining enumeration/count/value/reentry/throw assertions. The final passing log includes the previously unreachable checks. Controlled C ABI peers still do not prove real Rust payload admission.

## Codec-only control and interpretation

The driver is suitable for the bounded **old/new generated-encoder diagnostic**. It directly invokes `encode_by_id(34)` from separate original/current RN translation units. The build-control script uses the same header, Hermes dependencies, arm64 Simulator target, C++20, `-O3`, and `-fno-lto` for both. The unchanged RN header also matches its archived baseline.

The driver parses/loads input and reference before timing, checks the entire request against the generated TS codec before warmup and after measurement, and creates, consumes, and destroys a fresh Writer on every timed iteration. Its fixed 3 warmup / 31 measured / 16-encode schedule and all raw batch means are explicit. The unused decoder dependency throws if called. With separate translation units and no LTO, this is not a substituted encoder or an output-elision microbenchmark. The driver SHA-256 matches `8aebb039ad064ef64fcf0b6b9810a6a0d6ff3cd4b43fbaf32e94b59aa919632d`.

The preparation script imports the actual unchanged `FIXTURES`/`makeTree` and generated `parityEchoCodec`; all source, input JSON, wire hashes and four recorded wire sizes match the current files. It writes the complete command request, including command ID. The reference is independent of the changed C++ storage implementation, though it is another generated codec rather than a real Rust execution oracle.

One interpretation limit must remain explicit: JSON serialization drops `note: undefined` on even nodes, and Hermes `JSON.parse` reconstructs object layouts rather than executing the app's original `makeTree`. Optional wire semantics are preserved and both A/B sides receive the same parsed input, so this does not invalidate the diagnostic. It does prevent treating its latency as an exact reproduction of the public JS construction/object-shape path.

No timings or allocation counts were assessed here. The existing four fixtures all have two-entry metadata maps, so this diagnostic targets the inline path; it does not establish performance for maps above four entries. The parent must preserve source/binary/environment identities, independent launch ordering and raw results, then apply the planned real Rust/public iOS and Android checks before adoption. Full public round-trip, output reconstruction, real payload limits, and Nitro parity remain outside this codec-only control.
